name: sweet potato cornbread
instructions:
From Anita Spring Councel, 'Southern Roots' (p. 54). Captured verbatim from the source. The sweet potato adds a moist and tender texture along with a natural sweetness to traditional corn bread. Eat the corn bread on its own or sliced and filled with thinly sliced Southern dry-cured country ham or Italian paper-thin prosciutto. Each bite offers a delicious harmony of sweet and savory. This simple pairing transforms comforting sweet potato corn bread into a satisfying handheld snack. The choice is yours: Southern tradition or Italian tradition.

SERVES 6.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- 1 cup all-purpose flour
- 1/2 cup cornmeal
- 1/4 cup sugar
- 1 teaspoon baking powder
- 1/2 teaspoon baking soda
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1 teaspoon cinnamon
- 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg
- 4 tablespoons unsalted butter, chilled (OR salted butter — then omit the 1/2 tsp salt; see notes)
- 2 eggs, beaten
- 1 cup mashed, roasted sweet potatoes (about 1 large)
- 1 tablespoon finely grated orange zest
- 1/2 cup buttermilk (I use plain yogurt instead — usual substitution)

=== PROCEDURE ===

Preheat the oven to 350°F.

Grease an 8-by-8-inch baking pan. In a large bowl, stir together the flour, cornmeal, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg. Using a pastry cutter or your fingertips, cut the butter into the flour mixture.

In a separate medium bowl, mix together the eggs, sweet potatoes, orange zest, and buttermilk (or plain yogurt). Add the egg mixture to the flour mixture and stir together until combined.

Pour the batter into the prepared baking pan and bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until golden brown and the point of a knife inserted into the center comes out clean.
notes:
Source: Anita Spring Councel, 'Southern Roots', p. 54. Recipe captured as-is — flawless in original form.

PERSONAL SUBSTITUTIONS:
- PLAIN YOGURT in place of the 1/2 cup buttermilk. Standard buttermilk substitution.
- SALTED BUTTER + OMIT THE 1/2 TSP SALT — perfect swap. If you're using salted butter instead of the source's unsalted, drop the 1/2 tsp salt entirely; the salt in the butter carries the seasoning.
